data.name: Sample - NinjaOne - 1.0.0
data.description: Endpoint enrichment, exposure hunting, and gated patch remediation over the NinjaOne Public API v2.

workflows.name: NinjaOne - Enrich Asset
workflows.description: Resolve a hostname, IP, or logged-on user to a NinjaOne device and pull back its identity, owner, and a deep link to the console. This is the first step in almost every other flow, because every device operation takes the numeric NinjaOne device ID rather than a name.

arguments.note: No NinjaOne device matched. The host may be unmanaged, decommissioned, or known by another name.

routes.name: Get Device Detail -> Get Last User
Get Last User -> Get Console Link

workflows.name: NinjaOne - Find Exposed Endpoints
workflows.description: Given a product name from an advisory, answer "does this exist on our estate, and where is it unpatched?" -- the question a vulnerability workflow has to answer before anyone raises a ticket. Reads the estate-wide software inventory and the pending third-party patch report, so it needs no per-device iteration.

arguments.note: The product is not installed on any managed endpoint, so this advisory can be ruled out.

routes.name: Search Installed Software -> Search Pending Patches
Search Pending Patches -> Branch On Exposure
Branch On Exposure -> Installed And Current
routes.label: installed but patched

workflows.name: NinjaOne - Patch Endpoint with Approval
workflows.description: Show an analyst what is pending on one endpoint, ask for approval, then scan and apply. Requires OS and software patching to be enabled in the policy the device inherits, otherwise scan/apply return "patching is not enabled" -- a tenant setting, not a connector fault.

steps.name: Approve Patching
steps.description: **{{ vars.steps.List_Pending_OS_Patches | default([]) | length }}** OS patches and **{{ vars.steps.List_Pending_Software_Patches | default([]) | length }}** software patches are pending. Click **apply** to scan and install, or **skip** to leave it alone.

schema.title: Apply patches to this endpoint?
schema.description: **{{ vars.steps.List_Pending_OS_Patches | default([]) | length }}** OS patches and **{{ vars.steps.List_Pending_Software_Patches | default([]) | length }}** software patches are pending. Click **apply** to scan and install, or **skip** to leave it alone.

arguments.note: An analyst declined patching for this endpoint.

routes.name: List Pending OS Patches -> List Pending Software Patches
List Pending Software Patches -> Approve Patching
Scan OS Patches -> Scan Software Patches
Scan Software Patches -> Apply OS Patches
Apply OS Patches -> Apply Software Patches
Apply Software Patches -> Wait For Agent
Wait For Agent -> Check Running Jobs

workflows.name: NinjaOne - Reboot Endpoint with Approval
workflows.description: Ask before rebooting, suppress monitoring for the duration so the reboot does not raise its own alerts, reboot, then confirm the endpoint came back and lift the maintenance window.

steps.name: Approve Reboot
steps.description: Reboot **{{ vars.steps.Get_Endpoint.systemName }}** ({{ vars.steps.Get_Endpoint.nodeClass }})? The user will lose unsaved work.

schema.title: Reboot this endpoint?
schema.description: Reboot **{{ vars.steps.Get_Endpoint.data.systemName }}** ({{ vars.steps.Get_Endpoint.data.nodeClass }})? The user will lose unsaved work.

routes.name: Wait For Boot -> Check Back Online

workflows.name: NinjaOne - Restart Windows Service
workflows.description: Restart a named Windows service on an endpoint and verify it came back running. The usual response to a "service stopped" monitoring alert.

routes.name: Wait For Service -> Verify Service State
